available_scheduler_actions.description: Warm launch the top predicted app, then return HOME, when memory and thermal state are safe.
available_scheduler_actions.bit_value_contract: scheduler_bits[0] == 1 executes this exact pre-programmed action; 0 skips it.

available_scheduler_actions.description: Warm launch the second predicted app only when the current foreground context is idle enough.
available_scheduler_actions.bit_value_contract: scheduler_bits[1] == 1 executes this exact pre-programmed action; 0 skips it.

available_scheduler_actions.description: Ask lower-priority candidate apps to trim memory.
available_scheduler_actions.bit_value_contract: scheduler_bits[2] == 1 executes this exact pre-programmed action; 0 skips it.

available_scheduler_actions.description: Stop one safe, non-foreground, non-system, non-recommended background package only under memory pressure.
available_scheduler_actions.bit_value_contract: scheduler_bits[3] == 1 executes this exact pre-programmed action; 0 skips it.

available_scheduler_actions.description: Drop page cache only under critical memory pressure and root availability.
available_scheduler_actions.bit_value_contract: scheduler_bits[4] == 1 executes this exact pre-programmed action; 0 skips it.

available_scheduler_actions.description: Reduce warm-launch aggressiveness when SurfaceFlinger/RenderThread/UI evidence is busy.
available_scheduler_actions.bit_value_contract: scheduler_bits[7] == 1 executes this exact pre-programmed action; 0 skips it.

available_scheduler_actions.description: Avoid camera/media warmup under elevated thermal state.

context.scheduler_bit_contract: Return scheduler_bits as exactly 9 characters. Character i controls available_scheduler_actions[i]. Use 1 to execute the pre-programmed action and 0 to skip it.
context.required_output: Return strict JSON with top3_apps, pressure_analysis, scheduler_bits. Top-3 must be user-facing app categories from historical_app_categories or installed_apps, not OS-only labels.
context.scheduler_goal: Use device-side eBPF and system-state evidence to infer near-future Android app/resource demand, then choose safe warm-launch, cache, memory, network, camera/media, and UI scheduling actions.
